pattern.description: The multilingual ghost words fade out around the headline. The camera then accelerates into '32 languages.', scaling it until a gradient letter counter fills the frame. It passes through the letter and out into a new scene: an agent input card reading 'Welcome' with a gradient orb.
pattern.why_premium: The scene change uses the hero typography itself as the portal, so there is no cut. The gradient letter wipe carries the brand colours across the transition, and the accelerating scale (energy spike at the end) gives a punchy, physical sense of entering the product.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.ghostWords', {opacity: 0, x: -40, duration: 0.8, ease: 'none', stagger: 0.05}); tl.to('.headlineGroup', {scale: 30, transformOrigin: '62% 58%', filter: 'blur(4px)', duration: 0.55, ease: 'expo.in'}, '-=0.2'); tl.set('.headlineGroup', {opacity: 0}); tl.fromTo('.inputCard', {scale: 1.15, opacity: 0}, {scale: 1, opacity: 1, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power3.out'}); set the transformOrigin on the counter of the target glyph.
build_hint.remotion: The headline uses scale = interpolate(frame, [0, 17], [1, 30], {easing: Easing.in(Easing.exp)}) with transformOrigin at the glyph counter; it unmounts when scale > 25. The card uses spring({frame: frame - 17, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 180}}) for opacity and scale 1.15 to 1. The ghost words get a linear opacity fade and x drift.

notes: camera.move push_in (scale 2.67) here means the zoom-through on the type, followed by a new layout. The headline boxes b06 and b13 are fragments of the old headline area (it is gone from the end frame). The ghost-word texts are read from the filmstrip and should be checked for exact spelling (Hindi, Hungarian). The Turkish phrase also spans b05 and b04.
